correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the real Hermitian normal operator by Fourier orthogonality. With gain sqrt(t) on derivative intensities, its blocks are 5uuᵀ+3twwᵀ, two copies of [[5,5],[5,5+12t]], and two scalars 5. The diagonal block has trace 15+51t, product 390t of its nonzero eigenvalues, and kernel span(diag(3,-4,1)); the 2-by-2 blocks have trace 10+12t and determinant 60t. The kernel generator has rank three, which excludes every nonzero projector difference. Independently, put r=sqrt(985), R=(33+r)/4, d(t)=(15+51t+sqrt(225-30t+2601t²))/2 and c(t)=5+6t-sqrt(25+36t²). The full squared condition number is at least d(t)/c(t). At 40/81 these are the actual extreme positive eigenvalues and d=Rc. Their derivatives there are (51+1371/r)/2 and 6-96/r, respectively, so d−Rc has zero derivative there. The top affine-block eigenvalue d is convex and −c is strictly convex (the second derivative of sqrt(25+36t²) is positive); hence d−Rc is strictly positive elsewhere. Substitution gives the listed squared spectrum and multiplicities. For rank at most two, compress Q to the range of H and apply Cauchy–Schwarz: the compression has squared Frobenius norm at most 4²+3²=25 (the two largest eigenvalues of Q²), giving squared distance to span Q at least ||H||²_F/26. This proves the stated f/26 stability bound with f the least positive squared singular value. Read the supplied checker and transcript as recorded evidence; did not execute uploaded code.
residual_risks: No sharpness claimed on the projector-difference cone, nor beyond positive weights equal within each channel.
